title: Majority Element (Boyer–Moore Voting)
hints: Keep a candidate and a vote count; a zero count means pick a new candidate.
Verify the survivor actually appears more than n/2 times.
jsBridge: Boyer–Moore voting finds a candidate in O(1) space, then a second pass verifies it. Returning `Int?` makes "no majority" explicit, instead of JS's `undefined` or `-1`.

compass.q: Returning `-1` for "none" in JS clashes with a real `-1` value. How does `Int?` fix that?
Boyer–Moore vs a dictionary count: O(1) vs O(n) space. Does space matter on a phone?
Why is the verification pass required? Give an input where the candidate isn't a majority.
Consensus among sensor readings or votes: where could majority logic appear in an app?
